chapter: Opinions on players and ensemble jazz
title: Lakefront Lounge session assessment
summary: Allen and Rose recall the freewheeling Lakefront Lounge session and Burke's solo on Tishomingo.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: I've got about one minute. I don't know that we can really get into the things, but we were talking. While we were on these particular people, you had the lakefront lounges there. You had Sherwood, Dr. Bob Barber, Naki, Paul Crawford, there. What do you think of that session?

I think that's a fine session. That's one of the big kicks that I have to recall is the making of that session. It was a pretty freewheeling session, and I felt that we did a lot of very original material there. We had an original approach to things, and I think everybody liked it.
Yeah, I just wondered how it all fit together in your mind with that particular group of people,
if you felt it sounded like an ensemble? I think that it sounded enough like ensemble at the right times to satisfy me. It had a free sound, and I was very, very satisfied with that.
Yeah, well I enjoyed Raymond's solo sound, Tishomingo. Oh yeah. That was a terrific solo, as well as the band playing.
